questions.question: What does balance describe in a composition?
What is contrast?
choices: A repeated shape with no changes
A noticeable difference between visual elements

questions.question: How can emphasis guide a viewer?
choices: It makes one area or idea stand out

questions.question: What does rhythm create in visual art?
choices: A literal sound beat in every artwork
A sense of movement through repeated or varied elements

questions.question: What is pattern?
choices: A repeated decorative or structural design

questions.question: What does proportion compare?
choices: The relative size of parts to one another or to the whole

questions.question: How does unity contribute to a design?
choices: It makes every element the same size
It makes parts feel connected as a coherent whole

questions.question: What is variety in design?
choices: A strict repetition with no changes
A rule that removes focal points
Differences that add interest within a composition

questions.question: A poster's title is hard to notice. Which principle could improve it?
choices: Emphasis through stronger size, contrast, or placement

questions.question: What does movement describe in design?
choices: How a viewer's eye travels through the composition

questions.question: Which arrangement can create asymmetrical balance?
choices: Two identical halves reflected across a center
Different elements with visual weights that still feel stable
A design with no focal point

questions.question: Why might a designer use repetition with variation?
choices: To establish unity while keeping the composition engaging

questions.question: What does scale describe?
choices: The size of an element in relation to another or its surroundings

questions.question: A composition feels crowded. What revision may improve balance and clarity?
choices: Adjust spacing and visual weight among the elements

questions.question: How are contrast and emphasis related?
choices: Contrast can help create emphasis by making an element distinct

questions.question: What is an example of visual rhythm?
choices: A single object with no repetition
A note played in a song
A repeated sequence of shapes that leads the eye across a page

questions.question: Why is unity not the same as sameness?
choices: A unified design can connect varied elements through shared relationships
Unity requires all parts to be identical
Unity only occurs in symmetrical designs

questions.question: Which principle is most directly involved when a focal image dominates a layout?
How can negative space support a design's hierarchy?
choices: It removes the need for alignment
It separates groups and gives important content room to stand out

questions.question: What should an artist consider when choosing design principles?
choices: A fixed rule that all principles must be equal
The intended idea, audience, and relationships among visual elements
